newsitem.title: USA: Seattle-bound Amtrak train derails in Wyoming.
newsitem.headline: Seattle-bound Amtrak train derails in Wyoming.

text.p: An Amtrak passenger train en route from Chicago to Seattle derailed near Cheyenne, Wyoming, on Monday in bitterly cold temperatures, police and Amtrak officials said.
Amtrak spokeswoman Mary Ann Reynolds said nine of the 107 passengers aboard the "Pioneer" suffered "non-life-threatening" injuries and all but one had been treated and released.
Eleven of 12 cars derailed at 5:45 p.m. EDT (2245 GMT), Reynolds said, noting that none of the cars had overturned.
The derailment occurred about 18 miles (29 km) west of Cheyenne and passengers were taken by schoolbus to nearby hotels.
Amtrak has established a toll-free number for families of passengers to call: 800-523-9101.
